profile.label: Terrain analogy
profile.question: Which processed Earth windows match the reference window's landform shape (slope, local relief, roughness, relative elevation) at 60, 120 and 240 m?
required_measurements: Slope, local relief, roughness and relative-elevation distributions for both AOIs from integrity-checked DEMs at 60, 120 and 240 m
profile.ranking_conditions: Same reference AOI, terrain-v4.0, identical feature definitions, 60/120/240 m with a 1.2 km halo, equal family weights, SRTMGL1.003 for every Earth candidate.
profile.permitted_conclusion: This Earth AOI matches the selected planetary AOI on the measured terrain features at the tested scales under terrain-v4.0.

profile_state_reason: Every task-critical dimension is measured_comparable for every candidate, and all candidates share one eligibility key.
ordering_note: Tie groups (no ordering inside a group): Atacama Desert, Craters of the Moon lava field, Atacama Desert (south window), Hanksville badlands (MDRS), Meteor Crater (Barringer) | Upper Mustang, Ladakh. Base rate: 44% of 90 unselected Earth windows also score 99 or more, so a high terrain index is common for low-relief terrain. Ranking sensitive to method.

dimensions.label: Terrain and landform
dimensions.reason: terrain-v4.0: Wasserstein-1 distances between identically binned distributions at 60, 120 and 240 m, converted with S = 100·exp(−0.5·(W1/τ)²).

dimensions.label: Geology and mineralogy
dimensions.reason: A suitable public product exists but has not been processed for this AOI.
dimensions.earth_note: EMIT L2B mineral identification (EMITL2BMIN.001, NASA Earthdata login) or regional geological maps could support this, but nothing has been processed for this AOI and EMIT coverage of the exact window is unverified. A true-colour image is not mineral evidence.
dimensions.planetary_note: Jezero's units are mapped in USGS SIM 3464 (1:75,000). The mapped units have not been converted into a descriptor comparable with an Earth product.

sources.title: Sun & Stack (2020), Geologic map of Jezero crater and the Nili Planum region, Mars (USGS SIM 3464)
EMIT L2B Estimated Mineral Identification and Band Depth (EMITL2BMIN.001)

dimensions.reason: Shown as context only. It fails: spatial support, sampling equivalence. The two measurements do not answer the same question at the same scale.
dimensions.planetary_note: MEDA Thermal InfraRed Sensor (TIRS) · Mission sols 10–654 (first Mars year, all seasons)

checks.detail: MYD11A2.061 and mars2020_meda:data_calibrated_env (CAL_TIRS), both in kelvin.
Both are thermal-infrared retrievals of surface skin temperature (not air temperature). Emissivity assumptions differ between the retrievals.

Earth: mean of ~105 one-kilometre pixels over the 10 km AOI (~10⁸ m²). Mars: a few square metres beside the rover. Daytime skin temperature varies by tens of kelvin between sand, bedrock and dust at metre scale, so a point does not represent the window.
Day windows differ by 0.5 h and night windows by 0.4 h (gate: 1 h).
Earth: 44 paired 8-day composites over one year. Mars: 16 paired sols spanning Ls 11–358°.

Earth values are 8-day clear-sky composites, so cloudy conditions are excluded. Mars values are medians of single-sol 1-hour windows under all conditions, dust included. The two sampling schemes are not equivalent.
Earth 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z/2024-12-31T23:59:59Z; Mars Mission sols 10–654 (first Mars year, all seasons). Interannual variability is not characterised on either body.
MODIS QA ≤ 1 with LST error ≤ 2 K; MEDA rover still, low tilt, wheel and shadow flags.
24 sols used; rover position from NASA/JPL MMGIS waypoints on each sol.
Per-sample uncertainties are recorded but not propagated to the annual medians.

thermal_audit.summary: Shown as context only. It fails: spatial support, sampling equivalence. The two measurements do not answer the same question at the same scale.

checks.detail: MYD11A2.061 and mars2020_meda:data_calibrated_env (CAL_TIRS), both in kelvin.
Both are thermal-infrared retrievals of surface skin temperature (not air temperature). Emissivity assumptions differ between the retrievals.

Earth: mean of ~108 one-kilometre pixels over the 10 km AOI (~10⁸ m²). Mars: a few square metres beside the rover. Daytime skin temperature varies by tens of kelvin between sand, bedrock and dust at metre scale, so a point does not represent the window.
Day windows differ by 0.0 h and night windows by 0.0 h (gate: 1 h).
Earth: 41 paired 8-day composites over one year. Mars: 16 paired sols spanning Ls 11–358°.

Earth values are 8-day clear-sky composites, so cloudy conditions are excluded. Mars values are medians of single-sol 1-hour windows under all conditions, dust included. The two sampling schemes are not equivalent.
Earth 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z/2024-12-31T23:59:59Z; Mars Mission sols 10–654 (first Mars year, all seasons). Interannual variability is not characterised on either body.
MODIS QA ≤ 1 with LST error ≤ 2 K; MEDA rover still, low tilt, wheel and shadow flags.
24 sols used; rover position from NASA/JPL MMGIS waypoints on each sol.
Per-sample uncertainties are recorded but not propagated to the annual medians.

physical_limits: Surface pressure: Earth ~1013 hPa, Mars ~6 hPa (CO₂).
Mars has no global magnetic field and a thin atmosphere, so surface radiation is far higher.
Earth surfaces are shaped by liquid water, vegetation and biology that are absent on present-day Mars.

redundancy.interpretation: Values near 1 mean two families rank windows almost identically, so they add little independent evidence.

mola_vs_ctx.note: MOLA cannot validate the 60-240 m analysis scales; this compares regional slope only.

notice: Indices are similarity indices from 0 to 100 on the stated measurements. They are not probabilities, confidence levels, percentages of identity or complete planetary analogies.
